appendix.para: This section documents the significant changes made in each release. See the commits and pull requests on the repository for finer detail.

listitem.para: Closed . The code that checks for loops in the graph had catastrophically poor performance for a large number of nodes/edges. The fix for added additional edges to expression steps which caused the combinatorics to become readily apparent.

Closed (again). The code has been updated and more tests have been added. The approach now favors reporting the cause as a QName (a lexical QName with a colon), using a manufactured prefix if necessary.
Upgraded to Saxon 12.10 in version 3.0.50 but failed to note it in the change log.
Closed by making sure that the base URI is correctly set on inline documents. Previously, for XML documents, the base URI of the document element was always used.
Closed by making sure that typed maps and arrays work as parameters when p:run is called.
Closed by correctly reporting the error code for static errors encountered in stylesheets in p:xslt.

Closed by making sure that a single, atomic string result is a text/plain document. This change (temporarily) only applies to pipelines with version=3.2 because of backwards incompatibility consequences.
Closed . Don’t manufacture a prefix for error codes that are not in a namespace.
Closed . Make sure that the message option works on calls to user-defined steps.

Closed . Fixed p:xquery so the one-time configuration of the XQuery processor isn’t cleared by the reset method. Also added checks to make sure that reset and teardown don’t attempt to call the implementation if no implementation has been selected.
Closed by making sure that the reset method on p:http-request does clear its input documents.
Closed . Added dependencies to make it more likely that option initializing expressions will be evaluated “near” the step on which they are used.
Closed by making sure that the “no document properties are preserved” requirements are respected. Updated the test suite to add tests for correct behavior.

Closed by making sure that HTML documents get a proper document URI. (There’s a bug in the underlying HTML parser, but I’ve no hope for that being fixed. Instead, there’s a workaround.) I’ve also switched back to the version of the parser on Maven Central.
Closed . I’ve removed the BaseX distribution from the XML Calabash extension. This is possibly less convenient at first, but is less confusing when new versions of BaseX are released.
Added support for text value templates in comments and processing instructions.
Added missing functions, p:xpath-version-available and p:version-available.
Upgraded to Gradle 9.6.1. Fixed a bunch of Gradle features that raised deprecation warnings.
Updated to the latest version of the XProc test suite.

Implement the change to relative URI resolution for XProc 3.2. In steps labeled with version 3.2 or later, relative xs:anyURI options are resolved where they are specified (in the option shortcut or p:with-option), and not passed to a calling step as unresolved, relative URIs.

This was always the correct behavior according to the spec, but XML Calabash got it wrong. The community group decision to make this dependent on the version of the step is not ideal, but it will prevent existing pipelines from suddenly behaving differently.

Closed by upgrading the build script to Gradle 9.5.1 and the version of Kotlin to 2.3.21. This meant bumping the version of Java used in several places, but the class compatibility is not (supposed to have) changed. Cleaned up a few warnings identified by the new compiler.
Closed . Fixed a number of documentation errors in the description of the cx:asciidoctor step.
Closed . Fixed the AsciiDoctor PDF backend.
Closed . Added a default MIME type mapping for the .adoc extension to text/asciidoc.
Closed . Upgraded to Kotlin version 2.3.21 which (I hope) will fix the FreeBSD build problem.
Closed . Allow wildcards in the content-types values on inputs and outputs.
Closed . Detect context item references in nested function calls.
Closed . Rewrote the HTML document builder so that comments aren’t lost.
Closed . Allow XProc version 3.2 pipelines. Allow text value templates in comments and processing instructions in XProc 3.2 pipelines.
Upgraded to SchXslt2 version 1.11.1.
Added a set of PDF steps and a cx:tesseract OCR step. (“Some rabbit holes are deeper than others.”)
Closed . Report all of the (nested) causes when a pipeline fails with an exception.
Reorganized the test suite subprojects, mostly to improve the documentation. Added links from steps to corresponding tests in the test suite as a way of providing more usage examples.
Closed . Make sure that the initial query passed to BaseX has a base URI.
Closed . Put colons back in message reporter output.
Closed and . Fix message output on p:run and correctly handle static options passed to p:run.
Closed . Updated dependencies (Apache Commons Codec, Apache HTTP Client, Apache PDFBox, Jackson data formats, Jena, log4j-to-slf4j, Metadata extractor, PlantUML, Selenium-java, and XZ).
Closed . Configuration of CSS and XSL formatters was broken in several ways.
Closed and . Corrected errors related to non-element matches in p:viewport.
Closed . Output a debug-level message for unused variables.

Support several ways to set the value of serialization properties that accept a list of QNames as their value. Specifically, this applies to cdata-section-elements and suppress-indentation. They may be specified with a single string of space-separated URIQualifiedNames or as an XPath sequence containing one or more xs:QName values or strings containing single URIQualifiedNames.
Support static variables in serialization properties.
Added an extension feature for speculative XProc V.next features and implemented the p:document-class function.
Upgraded to SchXslt2 version 1.10.3.
Updated the version of the XProc test suite used to test the build.
Added links from the reference pages to additional examples in the XProc test suite.

Closed . Fixed the way document properties are serialized in MIME multiplexed output. This is backwards incompatible; document properties will be ignored in MIME output captured from XML Calabash versions before 3.0.45.
Closed . Fixed a typo in the configuration file schema (href is required on cc:catalog) and improved the documentation for the --catalog option.
Closed . Provide a proper error message for err:XD0052 (attempting to insert an attribute into a text value template).

Made several improvements to the “stacktrace” option. Fixed the bug where the stack trace only reported the last step; fixed the bug where --stacktrace and --debug were confused; documented the stacktrace configuration option.
Closed . Make sure configuration errors are caught and explained.

Closed . Abandoned attempts to avoid “empty” steps in the graph. The p:document (implicit or explicit) and p:inline bindings in a pipeline get promoted to “document” and “inline” steps. In a similar way, p:empty can be promoted to an “empty” step. As an optimization, rather than having “empty” steps, the ports were marked as “welded shut” requiring no input. This was also responsible for . I’ve removed this attempt at optimization, it’s not likely to have a noticable performance impact, but you will notice that pipeline graphs are different.

Closed . Corrected the way that arguments on the command line and arguments from the configuration file (cc:pipeline) are combined. There's a backwards-incompatible change here: if a pipeline URI is specified on the command line and it doesn't match the one specified on the cc:pipeline element, the configuration file settings are all ignored. Previously, they were used anyway.
Closed . Map the SVRL “fatal” severity to the XVRL “fatal-error” severity.
Closed . Make sure static options from imported libraries are in the set of in-scope variables for expressions in the importing step.
Upgraded to SchXslt2 version 1.10.2 which fixes a bug exercised by the test suites.
Closed . Avoid an index-out-of-bounds exception when decorated output is produced and a pipeline produces no output on a port.
Fixed the bug where the cx:assertions attribute was reported as unsupported on atomic steps.

Implemented the “ignore invalid URIs” extension feature. This feature enables a non-conformant mode where invalid URIs (such as “%gg” appearing in an xml:base attribute) are ignored rather than raising an error. It should be used only when absolutely necessary.

(As a purely practical matter, formatting the documents in the XProc test suite without this feature is nearly impossible because there are tests that intentionally contain invalid URIs to demonstrate that the processor will fail when it encounters them.)
Updated the project submodules to load the XProc test suite from the Codeberg repository.
Closed . Support the (not-yet-standard) options on p:xslt for template parameters.
Closed . Make sure that the encoding is passed to the HTML parser.
Closed . Improved XVRL reports from p:validate-with-schematron. Updated the step documentation.
Closed . Set the document element’s base URI when casting from text.
Closed . Read from stdin for an unbound primary input port only in --pipe mode.
Closed . Print the stderr output from p:os-exec at the “info” level if the step fails.
Closed . Improve error messages from Saxon by adding more detail. Also include error location in exception message when Trang fails.
Closed . Always set static options to compile-time values.
Upgraded SchXslt2 to version 1.10.1.
Updated build configuration; attempted to use Gradle 9.x, but it won’t build the Maven artifacts. Upgraded to 8.14 instead. And updated the foojay plugin.
Closed . Fixed a bug where tree construction failed if a processing instruction had a null base URI.
Improved versions reported for Jing, SchXslt, etc. (A format change meant they were being reported as “unknown”.)
Fixed a number of bugs in the new input, output, and multiplex options. Added an attempt to inform users if XML Calabash is waiting for input on the console.
Closed . Add xvrl:document to the xvrl:metadata when converting SVRL to XVRL.
Closed . Make sure that unbound ports on compound steps don’t cause problems at runtime.
Closed . Improve handling of console input and output. Updated the documentation about console handling.
Closed . Ignore the default readable port when configuring p:option defaults (options cannot have any bindings).

Closed and . Fixed line numbering and cx:cause in error reports. It’s no longer possible to load a pipeline that contains an xml:base attribute that’s syntactically invalid. Fixed an unrelated bug where p:run couldn’t appear in a p:try.

Closed . Improved the way a relative path is computed for two absolute URIs. Fixed the bug where the last slash was sometimes missing. Added support for paths that start at the root. Improved Windows path parsing (always compare drive letters case-insensitively).
Closed . Fixed presentation of xsl:message output. (It was really ugly and releases are cheap.)
Closed . Make sure that nodes selected from default inputs are documents not, for example, elements.
Closed . Don’t short circuit type checking for xs:string types, convert them to strings properly.
Closed and . Refactored output mechanisms to support several new features.

It is now possible to read and write MIME multipart/mixed encoded documents as input and output to pipelines. This allows the processor to write several documents to the same file in a way that allows them to be reliably parsed and reloaded. See --output, --input, --input-multiplex, --output-multiplex (and --temporary-files and --manifest).
Closed . Tidy up some warning messages and avoid an infinite loop in the error explainer.
Closed . Added cause to the c:error element produced by a p:catch.
Closed . Added tips to the documentation about the interaction between the line numbering feature and error messages from several steps.
Closed and . Attempt to improve error reporting.
Closed . Added some error explanation messages that were missing.
Closed . Resolved a few cases where namespace bindings could be incorrectly interpreted.
Fixed a bug where the cx:ditaa step always reported the result content type as image/png, irrespective of the content type actually selected.
Updated several dependencies to the most recent versions including SchXslt and NineML.

Closed . Repair damage done to xml:* attributes by the Validator.nu parser. It maps them all to names without colons. Added cx:xml-attributes to the parameters option for p:load (and consequently, p:document) to control the mapping, if necessary.
Closed . The release build is now based on Java 11. Java 17 was causing integration problems.
Closed . If cx:metadata-extractor fails, it should not write anything to the result port. (It was writing an empty document.)
Closed . Clarified the handling of QName values in attribute value templates (specifically on p:error). Improved the p:try step so that it adds a namespace binding if necessary for the error code.
Closed . Support passing multiple documents to p:catch on the error port.
Closed . Tidy up the MessageReporter interface. It’s better, but I think further improvements are possible.
Closed . Improved wording vis-a-vis the line-numbering option.
Closed . Fixed bugs related to type checking against the values list associated with an option.
Added the ability to cache compiled resources (stylesheets, queries, grammars. See Caching compiled resources.
Closed . Fixed a couple of errors related to handling nodes on the namespace axis.
Closed . Added reference documentation for the cx:use-catalog and cx:import-schema elements.
Closed . Fixed bugs in the handling of use-character-maps with respect to secondary result documents.
Closed . Made the cx:line-numbering parameter take precedence over any underlying Saxon configuration setting.
Closed . Fixed a bug when promoting a p:document instruction to a step when it happened not to have a default readable port.
Closed . Fixed a few places where the namespace bindings were not correctly applied in the XPL parser.
Closed . Added default media type mappings for .xhtm and .xhtml to application/xhtml+xml.
Closed . Correct the error that serialization properties in the documents were not taking precedence over properties provided on steps.
Closed . Fixed some confusion in the documentation vis-a-vis “line-numbers” vs. “line-numbering”.
Closed . Take more care with object state to avoid errors when steps are used in loops.
Closed . Fixed incorrect import URIs in the documentation.
Closed . Make sure p:wrap always returns documents with the content type application/xml.
Closed . Make sure that configuration-level changes to the serializer are protected from concurrent access.
Closed . Fixed a couple of bugs associated with setting line numbers using parameters; improved the documentation about the line numbering configuration. Added tests.
Closed . Support the line-numbering configuration option on the cc:xml-calabash element.
Closed . Make sure cc:mimetype elements update the processor correctly.
Closed . Added a URI resolver to the local BaseX processor; attempted to improve the documentation.
Updated the XML Resolver to version 6.0.21.
Closed . Remove optional dependencies from the POM.

Closed . When running a pipeline function from outside XML Calabash, copy the catalog files from the Saxon configuration into the XML Calabash configuration. This allows the pipeline function to use any -catalogs specified for Saxon.
Closed . Allow p:with-option to access its collection.
Closed . When the step option is used, make sure its library is validated. Also extends the --step option (and the step attribute on cc:pipeline) so that it can be either a name or a type.
This is a sooner-than-expected release, mostly because the documentation is broken in some browsers on some platforms and I think that may be intentional (on the part of the browser vendors).
Make sure you read the release notes for 3.0.33 if you haven’t already.
Closed . If attempting to parse an error page from a web server results in well-formedness (or other) errors, make sure the original error is reported, not the parsing error.
Added support for EXProc user-contributed pipelines. (The most-recent pipelines and the catalog are included in the release, so they can be used without loading the pipeline across the network.)
There are a few substantial changes in this release.
XML Calabash now requires Java 17 or later.
The XmlCalabashBuilder interface has been completely rewritten; that’s going to impact anyone integrating XML Calabash into another application.

A line numbering option has been added, this changes the default setting from “preserve line numbers in constructed documents” to “don’t preserve line numbers”. This will save memory and is usually not noticeable, though it may have an impact on some pipelines.
Closed . Upgraded to NineML version 3.3.4.
Closed . Corrected errors related to namespace bindings and option names. Also fixed the bug where an option in a namespace couldn’t be set with a shortcut.
Closed . Leveraging the XML Resolver in the document loader makes it possible to refer to resources in a ZIP file.
Closed . Moved DocumentServiceProvider initialization so it isn’t repeated.
Closed . Added a --line-numbering command line option and a corresponding configuration file setting.
Closed . Fixed (another) typo in the error explanations file.
Closed . Fixed the cx:xmlunit step by allowing it to construct the models it uses (rather than trying to cleverly wrap a DOM around the Saxon tree model).
Closed . All relevant command line options can now be set in the configuration file.
Fixed a bug where XML Catalog files provided on the command line were apparently not being used.
Improved the info mimetype command so that it can lookup extensions for a media type.
The documentation claimed that cc:xml-schema could have an inline schema document. This never worked and the schema and documentation have been updated to reflect this.
Added a cx:pebble extension step to run the Pebble templating engine.
Closed . Put the ex: prefix in the QName for the ex:epubcheck step.
Closed . Fixed the bug where the XMLn’t parser didn’t preserve the document base URI.
Closed . Fixed the bug where the XMLn’t parser didn’t correctly handle namespaces on the document element (or on unprefixed names).
Closed . Clarified the interpretation of sequences passed to pipeline functions. (Added a test to demonstrate the interpretation.)
Closed . Fixed another bug associated with default inputs. Track empty ports on a per-instance basis, not a per-type basis.
Closed . Fixed the output for text documents in the detailed visualizer.
Closed . Fixed the names of steps/ports in various err:XS0022 error messages.
Closed . When issuing SAX events directly from a parsed document, ignore comments if the LexicalHandler is null.
Closed . Make existing xml:base attributes absolute when using p:add-xml-base with relative set to false.
Closed . It isn’t practical to have step functions for atomic steps.

Fixed . Added code to construct SAX sources directly from trees. This allows location information to be preserved. (In principle, all of the steps that XProc provides would be implemented natively on top of our tree model. In practice, lots of steps use third party libraries and this results in trees being parsed twice. Previously, location information in the second parse would often be incorrect, from the user’s point of view, because the document being parsed is one that had already undergone attribute value normalization, might or might not have an XML declaration, etc.)
Fixed . Add location information to messages about compile-time type errors.
Fixed . Make sure that non-XML documents can be read from a ZIP file!
Fixed . Correctly handle JSON array documents passed to a pipeline function.
Fixed . Removed the unused “progress” value from the command line parser and help text for verbosity.
Fixed . Fixed a bug arising in a complex set of circumstances that could cause the processor to deadlock (hang). Added code to detect a deadlock and throw an error.
Fixed . Improve error messages when a user-defined error is raised.
Worked on . I’ve speculatively implemented a proposal from the ongoing discussion of how to clarify the semantics of the p:message step.

Added support for the dtd-attribute-values option on the p:validate-with-relax-ng step. (Hat tip to George Bina for the implementation work in Jing and for getting me out of the weeds in my attempts to use it.)
Added code to support recognizing the XVRL parameters passed to various flavors of validation step. They’re still ignored, but at least there’s a framework for recognizing them.
The message attribute is no longer allowed on p:declare-step. A declare step element is not a step invocation.
Updated to the latest 3.0 test suite.
Fixed . All output ports now appear in the result map when a pipeline function is called. If there was no output on a port, the map value will be the empty sequence.

Fixed . Text documents can now be passed to pipeline functions. An XML node value that contains only text is passed as a text/plain document, all other XML nodes are passed as application/xml. Maps, arrays, and scalar values are passed as application/json.
Fixed . Fixed p:step-available() so that it returns true for the standard compound steps, the extension compound steps, and p:run.
Fixed . Fixed p:text-head and p:text-tail so that they do end-of-line processing even when the line count is zero (meaning all the lines).
Fixed . Fixed a bug where the namespace bindings associated with a variable were resolved incorrectly.
Fixed . Fixed incorrect cross reference on the p:xinclude reference page. Corrected the way xml:id attributes are handled for pipeline fragments in the documentation.
Fixed . Improved the error message associated with passing an invalid option to a pipeline function. Generally improved error message handling for pipeline functions.
Fixed . Fixed a bug in how static options specified on the command line are handled. (Really fixed it this time, I think.)
Fixed . Corrected catastrophic error in command-line option handling.
Fixed . Fixed how map-valued options are handled on the command line.
Fixed . Clarified how steps are selected when the pipeline document is a p:library.
Fixed . Further improvements in the handling of exceptions in pipeline functions. If the exception detail is a document, serialize the document.
Fixed . Fixed a bug in how static options specified on the command line are handled.
Corrected documentation with respect to the (non-existant) --library option. (Thanks @galtm!).
Fixed . Added support for the c:compile parameter on p:validate-with-schematron.
Fixed . Added the AH control jar back into the distribution.
Fixed . Fixed a bug in the explanation for err:XD0036 when it’s caused by a type error in an XPath expression.
Fixed . Added a Java system property to identify the XML Calabash configuration when running pipeline functions starting outside of XProc.
Fixed . Improved error explanations and fixed some documentation issues.
Fixed . Suppress the “[No explanation for …]” message when --explain is used and the error is a user-defined error with no explanation.
Fixed . Improved the detail in exceptions thrown by pipeline functions.
Upgraded to SchXslt2 version 1.7.
Updated ex:expand-templates to allow text source documents.
Fixed . Updated to SInclude version 5.6.0. This fixes a bug where in-scope namespaces were lost that effected the documentation. Also updated a few other things.
Fixed . Fixed a bug where errors in “pipelineception” functions couldn’t be caught in XSLT or XQuery.
Fixed . Fixed a bug where expressions were not evaluated correctly when multithreading was used.
Fixed . Added p:run to the reference documentation.
Fixed . Make sure that input errors are cleared when a compound step is reset.
Fixed . Fixed a bug where calls to pipeline extension functions were treated as static, which they aren’t (in general).
Fixed . Improved rendering of AVTs in visualizer output.
Fixed . Improved xmlcalabash.ps1 so that it works correctly in both Powershell 5 and Powershell 7.
Added support for ex:epubcheck, that is, the EPUB check step in the EXProc namespace.
Added an ex:expand-templates step to expand attribute- and text-value templates in an input document. This is in the EXProc step namespace.
Made a variety of improvements to the polyglot steps.
Fixed typos in the reference documentation. (Thanks @galtm!)
Fixed . When the polyglot steps fail, the underlying exception is now passed back and included in the error output.
Fixed . Attempted to clean up the distribution jar files. The standard distribution contained a bunch of unnecessary jars related to extension steps.
Fixed . Corrected an error in the p:insert step that caused text/html inputs to be rejected.
Fixed . When a RELAX NG grammar is invalid, the underlying exception is now passed back and included in the error output.
Added support for Paged.js as a cx:css-formatter.

Fixed . Reworked the Maven dependencies so that Saxon-EE is no longer required. Also removed many of the dependencies needed for extension steps (for example, Selenium). All of the dependencies are still bundled with the released application, these changes only apply to projects that are using Maven dependencies to include XML Calabash.

Fixed . The initializers for static options are now always resolved statically, even if analysis can’t prove that the value can be resolved statically. This will result in errors if it can’t, but won’t result in null pointer exceptions if analysis fails. Also improved the analysis associated with p:system-property.
Fixed . There were still a number of errors related to the buffering message reporter necessary for cx:pipeline-messages.
Fixed . My update to use a buffering message reporter had the unintended consequence of suppressing all messages. I’ve done some emergency API surgery to “fix” it.
Fixed . Fix bugs in the handling of serialization properties for secondary result documents in p:xslt, especially character maps.

Fixed . Provide more details about where XPath/XSLT parsing errors occur; for example, the location of static errors in a stylesheet. This fix improves the situation, but further work may be required.

Fixed . Use a buffering message reporter in the main application. The cx:pipeline-messages step relies on a buffering message reporter. The test driver was using one, but the main application was not.
Fixed . Support parameters on the p:schematron step. Only SchXslt2 parameters are supported.
Upgraded Schematron support to SchXslt2 version 1.5.
Fixed . Make sure a reasonable error is reported for a top-level pipeline that contains no steps.
Fixed . FOP has a completely broken implementation of URI resolution against the base URI; worked around that. Also added an event listener so that FOP messages are reported.
Fixed and . There were a couple of issues relating to static options. At least one is likely to be better resolved when the refactor for is finished.
Fixed . Allow the pipeline specified on the command line to be a URI.
Fixed . Fixed a bug in transformation of SVRL to XVRL caused by a missing namespace declaration.
Fixed . Fixed a bug where setting the trace output to a simple filename, without a path, caused an error.
Fixed . Make sure proxy settings are passed all the way through to the runtime configuration.
Fixed . Make sure that a warning message is printed if the user attempts to use graph output but hasn’t configured Graphviz.
In the p:os-info step, added all the properties to the cx: namespace, even the standard ones (that are also reported without a namespace).
Upgraded to EPUBCheck version 5.3.0.
Fixed . The XMLn’t parser wasn’t recognizing the built-in xml: prefix.

Fixed . The p:validate-with-relax-ng step was failing to use the catalog resolver. It was also using the wrong URI (the document URI instead of the schema URI) in error messages about schema problems.
Fixed . The command line mechanism for setting the content type of a source document only worked for stdin.
Fixed . Improved error messages associated with unsuccessful attempts to parse with p:invisible-xml. The error message now includes the failed parse, if there is one.
Fixed . Remove non-static options from the set of in-scope variables when a p:declare-step is nested inside another step declaration.

Fixed . Corrected a couple of bugs in p:send-mail. Generalized the properties that can be set with cc:send-mail. Improved the documentation and specifically included an example of how to send mail with a modern TLS-enabled system.
Fixed . Support for pipeline functions failed to consider the possibility that a step might have no inputs, outputs, or options.
Fixed . Several bugs related to the scope of pipeline functions have been fixed. New tests have been added.
Fixed . Added tests and documentation for running pipelines as functions.
Upgraded to Saxon 12.9.
Fixed . Improvements to the XMLn’t parser: handle entity references in attribute values, support include and ignore marked sections in the external subset, improved some error messages.
Fixed . Updated the xmlcalabash.sh script in the distribution to use a POSIX-compliant version of “readlink”.
Added support for the XMLn’t parser.
Fixed . The command line application (the “main” class) should now be available from maven as com.xmlcalabash:xmlcalabash:app.
Fixed . The message attribute is now supported on compound steps.
Fixed . This was another bug related to the output of p:try. Also fixed a couple of small errors related to the base URI of inlines.
Fixed . Added a cx:elemental step. At present, this is using the same REST API as the cx:exist-db step; but if the APIs diverge in the future, it’ll be clear which one is intended.
Fixed . It is now possible to set static parameters on p:xslt.

Fixed . I’ve made another attempt at resolving the encoding problems on Windows console output. As far as I can tell, the root cause here is that in Java 18, the default character set was changed to UTF-8, irrespective of the platform. So if you run XML Calabash with Java 18+ on Windows, Java says the default character set is UTF-8 and it often just isn’t.

The current workaround is to use -Dfile.encoding=COMPAT if no explicit file.encoding property is specified. That gives backwards-compatible behavior. If that doesn’t work, using -Dfile.encoding to pass the actual, correct encoding should.
Fixed . An explicitly named output port on a p:try step was misinterpreted as a static error.
Fixed . Preemptive authentication on p:http-request has never actually worked.

Fixed and . Added support for processing XQuery using BaseX or eXist-db. This support is available through cx:basex and cx:exist-db steps. It is also possible to make either implementation the default processor for p:xquery steps.
The steps that implement BaseX or eXist-db processing are distributed separately and must be added to your classpath.
Fixed and . The interactive debugger now supports tab completion. Also fixed the bug where sometimes “exit” had to be entered twice in order to quit the debugger.
Fixed . Highlighting of step names in the graph visualization output is improved.
Fixed . Upgraded to a more recent version of the DocBook xslTNG stylesheets for formatting the documentation. This fixes an ugly accessibility issue related to the spacebar.
The “info version” command now identifies the JVM default character set.
Switched to version 5.5.0 of SInclude, the XInclude processor.
Fixed . Output filenames had incorrectly formatted extensions in the detailed trace listener.
Fixed and . Made a couple of small changes to the p:css-formatter step.
Fixed . Added a store command to the interactive debugger.
Fixed . Attempted to improve the documentation in the language reference. More improvements can surely be made.
Updated Schematron implementation to SchXslt2 version 1.4.4.
Updated dependencies and the way dependencies are managed. Updates:
ch.qos.logback:logback-classic from 1.5.13 to 1.5.18
com.fasterxml.jackson.* from 2.18.2 to 2.19.2
com.github.f4b6a3:uuid-creator from 6.0.0 to 6.1.1
com.networknt:json-schema-validator from 1.5.4 to 1.5.8
com.princexml:prince-java-wrapper from 1.3.0 to 1.5.0
commons-codec:commons-codec from 1.17.0 to 1.19.0
de.bottlecaps.ebnf-convert:ebnf-convert-lib from 0.70 to 0.72
de.bottlecaps.rr:rr-lib from 2.1 to 2.5
net.minidev:json-smart from 2.5.1 to 2.5.2
net.sourceforge.plantuml:plantuml from 1.2025.2 to 1.2025.4
org.apache.commons:commons-compress from 1.27.1 to 1.28.0
org.apache.httpcomponents.client5:httpclient5 from 5.3.1 to 5.5
org.apache.jena:* from 5.3.0 to 5.5.0
org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-to-slf4j from 2.23.1 to 2.25.1
org.apache.pdfbox:* from 2.0.32 to 3.0.5
org.apache.xmlgraphics:fop from 2.10 to 2.11
org.jline:* from 3.28.0 to 3.30.4
org.seleniumhq.selenium:selenium-java from 4.28.1 to 4.34.0
org.slf4j:slf4j-api from 2.0.16 to 2.0.17
org.w3c:epubcheck from 5.0.1 to 5.2.1
org.xmlresolver:xmlresolver from 6.0.17 to 6.0.19
org.xmlunit:xmlunit-core from 2.10.0 to 2.10.3
Call this the “Balisage 2025” release. Hopefully, I won’t decide anything else needs fixing before my talk next week. It’s a “.13” release, but you’re not superstitious, right?
Fixed by making sure that the default readable port is applied correctly to the cx:until and cx:while steps.
Added examples to the language reference.

Fixed . Added a language reference chapter that includes at least a brief summary of all the XProc elements. This also improves the documentation for the XML Calabash extension steps, cx:until and cx:while.

Fixed . The source input on p:invisible-xml is now unconditionally treated as a string. Note that there’s another wrinkle here, the select expression “something/string()” is an application/json document containing a single string atomic value. The expression “something/text()” is a text/plain document containing a single text node. That’s a sharper edge than we might like.

Fixed . Use the JVM default charset encoding for console output. The console-output-encoding configuration option has been removed and XML Calabash now tries harder to use the JVM’s default charset for console output. The helloWorld.xpl sample pipeline has been extended to print some Unicode characters and the installation chapter has been extended to describe encoding issues in more detail.

Fixed . Improved the PowerShell script so that it attempts provide command line arguments in a more useful format. (Left to its own devices, PowerShell splits arguments on “:” which is inconvenient for XML Calabash.) Also added support for checking the $env:JAVA_HOME environment variable in PowerShell.

Attempted to make it easier to get debug information. Added an example logback-debug.xml file to the lib directory in the distribution. This configuration prints debug messages to the console and saves them in a file named xmlcalabash.log. The included scripts for running XML Calabash have also been improved so that arguments of the form “-D…” are recognized as Java property settings and added to the command line in the right place. (Note that on Windows, you have to quote any property setting that includes a “.”, for example '-Dlogback.configurationFile=lib/logback-debug.xml')
Improved the --debug option and the documentation for the option. They’re now better aligned.
Various small documentation and documentation build fixes.
Fixed and . Data models constructed for non-XML inputs were accidentally using the base URI of the static context as their base URI instead of their actual base URI.
Fixed . Added a default MIME type mapping for the .xspec extension.
Migrated to Saxon 12.8 and updated to the latest XProc 3.0 test suite.
Fixed . Make sure that trace output is saved even if the pipeline fails.
Fixed . Clarify the error messages for err:XD0006 and err:XD0007 so that the user can distinguish between “no documents” and “more than one document”.
Fixed . Support XML grammars on p:invisible-xml. At the moment, this only works with the NineML implementation of Invisible XML.

Fixed . Correct the documentation for output filespecs. Apparently, I implemented them using the rules of “String.format” and documented them as if I’d used the rules of “fn:format-number”. Hilarity ensued. I also changed the implementation so that multiple outputs to a single file are concatenated together as the documentation indicates. Previously, each new document overwrote the previous.

Fixed . Previously, no attempt was made to preserve character maps from XSLT steps and there was no mechanism for setting character maps at the XProc level. Character maps are now supported using the same direct mapping format as the fn:serialize function. They’re also saved as part of the serialization properties on output ports, for example from p:xslt. Finally, there are a couple of bugs in Saxon and XML Calabash now works around those.
Fixed . Make sure the .dot files are explicitly closed so that they are readable on Windows. Also corrected errors in the way logging was handled by the visualizer class.
Fixed . Removed the “this is alpha software” admonitions from the documentation. That’s only a little bit terrifying.
Fixed . Attempting to copy or move a file onto itself is an error.
Fixed , Java 11 should be sufficient again. I switched back to the previous method of selecting a toolchain for the build. This seems to work, though I can’t really explain why.
Related to , added the eager-uri-resolution feature.

Fixed . Make sure --output filenames are parsed correctly. Output filenames are now explicitly made absolute against the current working directory. If a URI is given as the filename, it must be a file: URI. Attempted to clarify the documentation.
Fixed . Make sure the base URI is propagated into XSLT result documents.
Fixed . Use only the first input as the context item when processing a sequence with XSLT 2.0.
Fixed p:urify() so that it passes nw-urify-non-windows-bs-002. I had at one time argued for a change in behavior, but I gave up.
There were a bunch of build-related changes trying to get CI to do the right thing and publish releases with JReleaser.

Fixed . Escape “[” and “]” in URIs. This is the simplest fix for the bug where a file named [Content_Types].xml in a zip file causes p:archive-manifest to fail. The java.net.URI class won’t make a URI that contains square brackets. There are other reserved characters it doesn’t care about, so I’m not sure if there’s a better, proper solution.
Fixed . Make sure the module URI resolver is configured for the p:xquery step.

Fixed . Make sure that namespace bindings are setup correctly. Several steps were capable of producing apparently valid XDM results that did not serialize correctly because the namespace bindings were not up-to-date.
Test suites are now published automatically at . This provides some examples of usage, especially for extension steps.
Fixed . On Windows, the p:urify() function didn’t handle “/C:/path/to/file” correctly.
Fixed . Made the XML Schema module URI resolver do the right thing.
Fixed . Added support for setting serialization parameters on the command line.

Fixed . Corrected several errors in option handling. Static options that did not have an initializer were not recognized and options passed from the command line applied to all steps, not just the outer-most step.
Fixed . Resolved a performance issue during graph construction.
Fixed . Corrected an error in the test driver.
Added the cx:fileset step, inspired by Ant FileSets.
Fixed a bug in the way document properties were handled when using select on p:with-input.
Updated the Schematron implementation to SchXslt2 version 1.3.5.
Fixed . Make sure that the path used for include/exclude matching in p:directory-list is correct. (Removes a spurious leading “/”.)
Fixed . Enable logging for warnings and errors. This got disabled accidentally at some point.
Fixed . Preserve document properties when doing selections. This is an attempt to address issue #1156 from the specification.
Fixed . If no specific XSL processor is requested, use FOP by default.
Fixed . Allow text documents on the insertion and result ports of p:insert.
Fixed . Make the content type of “.md” files text/markdown by default.
Fixed where p:file-copy sometimes acted like p:file-move and removed the originals!
Fixed . Make the result port on p:compare primary!
Updated the cx:selenium step:
Added an “until different” clause to the find statement
Fixed a bug in the grammar of the send statement
Bumped the grammar version from 0.2 to 0.3
Version 0.2 grammars are compatible with 0.3 and still accepted
Added more debugging statements to the cx:selenium step
Make the default assertion level “ignore” not “warning”.

revdescription.para: The big change here is moving from GitHub to Codeberg.

listitem.para: Fixed . Added support for the version attribute on cc:xml-calabash. Improved the messages associated with errors in the configuration file.
Fixed . Fixed a bug that caused p:run inside a loop to “get stuck” because of a problem with how input ports were handled.
Fixed . Fix Windows platform dependencies in xmlcalabash.ps1. There’s another bug with piped input, but it’s not clear how to fix that.
Fixed . Cleaned up some of the implementation details in the p:invisible-xml step.
Fixed . Set the default content type for .ixml files to text/plain.

revdescription.para: (The beta6 release never actually got published because I forgot to tag it.)

listitem.para: Fixed . Make sure that user-supplied values for static options are used during compilation.

Refactored the paged media steps into the main build. Along the way, I discovered that Prince XML has an artifact in Maven Central, so I switched to that API. The available options for the Prince XML-backed p:css-formatter step have changed; some of those changes are backwards incompatible.

Restructured code and tests for running in a set of Docker containers. The idea is to be able to run testing and release tasks in containers so that there’s no “bleed through” of the local development environment.
Moved to the new Maven Central repository using the legacy OSSRH APIs.

revdescription.para: For some reason, it appears that snapshots aren’t being updated after they’re created. The build runs without error, and claims to publish the snapshot, but the files on Maven don’t get updated. I don’t know why.

listitem.para: Fixed . Make sure that line numbering is enabled for pipelines constructed from a Source.

Substantial build refactoring. All of the extension steps, except the Polyglot steps that require Java 17 and the paged media steps that mostly require third party applications, are now part the main build instead of being subprojects. This should simplify things a bit. It did have a knock on effect of changing some of the documentation build. For the better, I hope.
Fixed . Make sure that static options are evalated with the correct context.
Fixed . Handle the case where the only command given is “info”.
Re-re-fixed . Once again, the problem was in the XInclude processor, now bumped to version 5.4.1. This time I wrote a fairly extensive test case to “prove” it works correctly.
Fixed . Allow (API) users to add custom Saxon configurers with XmlCalabashBuilder.
Fixed . Reverted the fix that added a warning message about non-node inputs to p:xslt. It was unreliable.
Fixed . Added an info command that can display information about the known mimetypes.
Fixed . Added .xqm, .xquery, and .xql as standard filename extensions for application/xquery files.

revdescription.para: I wasn’t really planning to do another release today, but there are some nice usability improvements in here and releases are cheap…

listitem.para: Fixed . Improved the error messages reported when stylesheet compilation fails for a p:xslt step.
Fixed . Allow the port name to be omitted for input and output ports on the command line if the pipeline has only a single such port.
Fixed . Fixed a bug where the serialization option on the p:store step was not taking precedence.
Fixed . If you attempt to process a stylesheet without passing an initial template name, and if the input is not a node, it will often silently fail. Output a debug message warning of this fact.
Fixed . Improved the error message associated with a p:pipe as a child of p:input.
Fixed . Fixed the error location for dynamic errors in atomic steps. (Previously, the location of the containing compound step was always reported.)
Fixed . Make sure that the document manager is used as the resource resolver for step processing.
Fixed . Make sure that the global context item, and other properties, are correctly reset when p:xslt is used in a loop.
Fixed . Support constructing a pipeline from a java.xml.transform.Source.

Support XML input to the cx:selenium step. Also did some IDE-directed code cleanup in the step itself. There’s a (currently undocumented) RELAX NG grammar for the XML input. It’s possibly a bit sketchy. And the step doesn’t validate the input.
Fixed . Improved the error message associated with attempts to connect to an unknown port.
Fixed . Make sure that options are set to their typed values.
Fixed . Apply serialization properties specified in the configuration file.
Fixed . Fixed a bug where “null” would sometimes appear in the graph visualization.
Fixed (again). Updated the XInclude processor to 5.4.0 to correct a bug where nested base URIs were not correctly preserved.

revdescription.para: If I’m going to get a couple of betas out in May, I best get started, eh?

listitem.para: Fixed . The xsl:messages from stylesheets run with p:xslt are output at “info” level. (They were accidentally getting discarded in the last few alphas.)
Fixed . Make sure that option shortcut values are stored as untyped atomic values so that they can be promoted to the appropriate type.
Fixed . Refactored build and configuration APIs.
Fixed . Removed some debugging code that always printed a JVM stack trace when p:run failed.
Fixed . Refactored the DocumentManager API.
Added cx:jsonpath and cx:find extension steps.
Added cx:json-diff and cx:json-patch extension steps.
Made a number of improvements to error reporting.
Improved error messages for documents that can’t be parsed. (Previously, “file not found” would be reported in some circumstances.)
Improved error message when content type shortcuts are used in inappropriate places.
Fixed a bug where the underlying cause of an exception sometimes got lost in nested exceptions. When a pipeline fails, the error report now includes the chain of causes.
Clarified the error message for the special case of empty sequence in a type conversion error.
Added a --stacktrace option to enable stack (step) traces in errors (and disabled them by default).
Improved the formatting of error explanations when the --explain option is used.

Fixed . Make sure that options passed on the command line are promoted as required. (So “true” can be used for an xs:boolean value.) Also changed the error code used for option values that don’t match (or can’t be promoted to) the correct type. They now raise err:XD0036 instead of err:XS0077 which is really about attribute values not option values.
Fixed . Make sure the default verbosity is “info”, not “warn”. (This error was introduced while tinkering with the logging code; it was probably never released.)

Fixed . Restore loading ~/.xmlcalabash3 as the default configuration file if no configuration is given explicitly and if ./.xmlcalabash3 doesn’t exist. (In alpha31 or alpha32, the code to load ~/.xmlcalabash3 was lost, now it’s back.)

Disabled standard Java logging to stderr. This seems a bit odd, but XML Calabash has its own error reporter (necessary so that pipelines and integrators can capture the error messages). That reporter sends all messages to the standard Java logging system. That’s necessary so that it’s possible to capture lower level debug messages to a file without sending them all to the console. But it means that if an error occurs, the reporter prints the error message and then the underlying Java logging system prints it again, in a slightly different format. That’s going to be both confusing and annoying, so by default no Java log messages are printed.
Significant refactoring of message and logging systems.

There’s more separation between things that are logged through the message reporter and things that are only logged to the underlying Java logger. The intent is that things only relevant to debugging XML Calabash go only to the logger. Things that might be relevant to debugging a pipeline go to both places.

One exception is that details about how the application is configured go only to the underlying Java logger. This is necessary because we haven’t configured a message reporter before we’ve configured the application!
The default logback.xml configuration file has been simplified. It no longer uses dynamic configuration. Use a different configuration file to change the level.
The error explanation implementation has been changed so that it also uses the message reporter, rather than writing directly to stderr.
Multithreaded execution complicates the task the visualizer is trying to perform. The “detail” visualizer has been updated.
Fixed a few bugs in the cx:wait-for-update step; it didn’t work reliably for HTTP URIs.
Fixed . Improved the conformance of p:import-functions. Private functions are now excluded and nested imports are handled correctly.

Fixed . Corrected errors in p:os-exec. Fixed the bug where output to stdout was discarded unless the process ended with a return code of zero. Serialization properties and output charsets are now handled correctly.
Fixed . Remove carriage returns from p:os-exec output on Windows.
Fixed . The cwd option on p:os-exec is handled correctly if it’s a URI.
Fixed . Reworked the DocumentManager API.
Fixed . Added support for the language attribute on the XVRL schema element.
XML Calabash now uses Saxon 12.6 by default.

The Windows-related fixes in 3.0.0-alpha29 weren’t wholly satisfactory. Some places where those fixes were incomplete have been refactored. (I think two issues had been conflated and their union fixed, leaving each of the individual problems only partially resolved.)
Fixed . Make sure that attempts to get a path from a file: URI deal with irregularities on Windows.
Fixed . Don’t print “Stack trace:” on errors if there’s no stack trace.
Refactored the MessageReporter API. More information is now available to aid other presentation formats, localization requirements, etc.
This release is a handful of small bug fixes, many related to tidying up loose ends in Windows functionality. Essentially all of the test suite tests now pass on Windows.
Fixed . Don’t put leading slash or, on Windows, drive letters in ZIP archive names. This change applies across all the archive formats, for consistency.
Fixed . Removed the spurious “:” from the start of message output on steps.

Made a variety of changes to improve functionality on Windows: make sure files get closed, sort out some edge cases with Windows filenames, corrected a few tests that depended on end-of-line characters, fixed a bug in p:file-create-tempfile (it returned the path instead of a URI).
Added the ability to run pipeline steps in parallel (“multi threading”). This required a substantial bit of refactoring. I think it works correctly. See Running steps in parallel.

Fixed . Improved the presentation of error output to address a comment on the mailing list. I’ve also made the error output from the p:xslt and p:xquery steps more informative (and generally fixed a few loose ends in the p:xquery step).
Fixed . Corrected a typo that prevented “?” from being correctly escaped in p:urify.
Fixed . Static options imported in a common library (one imported by several other libraries) no longer get flagged as illegal duplicates.
Fixed . Somewhere along the line, I broke the --verbosity option so that it had no effect on the output. Now it does again.
Fixed . Added a shortcut for setting map parameters on the command line.
Fixed and made a number of other improvements in the test driver.

Fixed by improving the p:urify function. This is a little bit speculative as xproc/#1145 is still being discussed. But the current behavior is so fundamentally broken that I’m making a few proactive fixes. These changes also mean that p:urify is implicitly called in many places which should also help on Windows.
Fixed . Added support for content-types in the document cache. You can now cache the same document parsed with different content types.
Added some new unit tests to demonstrate programmatic use of XML Calabash from your own JVM application.
Fixed a bug where it wasn’t possible to set the value of a pipeline option named “message”. This was an accidental consequence of how the message attribute is handled on compound steps.

Added a stack trace to the error output. If a step fails, the default error reporter now prints a “stack trace” showing the step that failed and the steps it was nested inside. If this turns out to be annoying, I’ll add a configuration option to turn it off.

Fixed several bugs in the implicit validation feature. Implicit validation was accidentally enabled by default and there were also some issues with correct handling of the base URI when the base URI was explicitly absent.
Fixed several, small bugs in the SVG visualizer.

The big (as in “sweeping” and arguably a little riskier than most recent updates) fix in this release is a substantial refactor of the core of the application. This was partly done to clean up the API for creating a processor, and partly because I had outstanding concerns about the previous big refactor from about a year ago. It’s a mostly not-visible change if you’re just using the command line application, but there was at least one bug fix where the document properties of a variable were wrong (the tests passed by accident).
Fixed . The SVG output doesn’t display options on steps that have no binding. They still have a binding to the empty sequence, but the diagram is a lot less cluttered without them.
Fixed . The graph visualizer was completely unprepared for connections to option expressions.

Fixed by sending message output to standard error instead of standard output. This assures that message output and pipeline output don’t clash. Writing to standard error should probably have been the default from the beginning.
Fixed . Documentation improvements; step names are now links to the appropriate reference page.
(Re)fixed . Make sure that the global context item is initialized (so that the custom stylesheet can define global variables).

Fixed . Attempted to improve the way writing pipeline output to standard output is handled. Pipeline output to standard output is “undecorated” if only one port is being output and it cannot produce a sequence.
I made some aesthetic improvements, well, changes at least, to the SVG graph styling: curved borders, a few colors.
Added cx:trang and cx:trang-files steps.
Fixed . The regular expression used to match the URI scheme was woefully inadequate.

Fixed by supporting an explicit syntax for specifying the content type of inputs specified on the command line. This is especially relevant when reading from standard input as the name gives no hints about the content type.
Fixed . This release includes a substantial revision to SVG diagrams of pipelines and graphs. This has no user-visible effects unless you’re interested in styling the SVG diagrams.
Fixed by documenting the --nogo option.
Fixed by documenting the format option values for p:archive and p:unarchive.

Fixed by detecting errors in expressions at run time. Static errors in expressions now generate a warning at compile time and a failure at runtime. I’m not convinced that’s exactly right, but it does mean that a static error in an expression that’s never evaluated won’t raise an error.

Fixed . The way that SVG diagrams are generated for pipelines and graphs has been more-or-less completely rewritten. The XML description of pipelines and graphs are now broadly similar. Almost all of the styling is performed by XSLT and there’s a mechanism for users to provide their own stylesheets. The documentation has been updated to (attempt to?) explain how this works.
The pages generated by the --graphs option have been updated to improve the presentation and navigation.
A number of small changes have been made in several places to try to provide the pipeline description with more information about the steps and the connections between them.
A new --nogo option has been added. This option compiles the pipeline and generates the graphs, if requested, but does not attempt to run the pipeline.
Fixed by making the source port on cx:sparql primary. (That was an oversight in the library that declares the step.)
Fixed by making sure that p:directory-list paths are normalized against the base URI correctly.

Fixed by making sure that secondary (non-primary) input ports are bound correctly. A secondary input is not bound to the default readable port if there’s no explicit connection for it. Instead, it’s bound to the input port’s default connection.
Fixed by documenting that using an extension step requires providing its declaration; added a the library URIs to all of the extension step reference pages.
Fixed by bundling CoffeeSacks with XML Calabash (this is the Saxon extension function for Invisible XML). The function is automatically registered.
Added support for user-styling of the SVG pipeline and graph output. Documentation T.B.D. (See .)
Added (somewhat experimental) support for implicit XML Schema validation of primary inputs.

Updated Apache FOP support; XML Calabash is now using FOP 2.10. Added image/png, image/tiff, application/X-fop-areatree, and application/vnd.hp-PCL as output formats. Allow image/svg+xml as an output format, but note that it requires a build of FOP with the sandbox enabled.
Added support for the p:message step.
Fixed by forbidding the [p:]message attribute from being specified with p:with-option. (It’s not an option.)
Fixed (and ). All of the extension steps (except for the polyglot steps) are now bundled into the distribution.
Fixed . Make sure that [p:]message attributes on user-defined steps are output when the steps are run.
Fixed by making IDs explicit so that Graphviz doesn’t output duplicates in the SVG. Cleaned up the graph output in a few small ways.

Fixed . Added cx:ebnf-convert, a wrapper around Gunther Rademacher’s EBNF converter, and updated cx:railroad to use it directly. This will make it easier to draw railroad diagrams of, for example, Invisible XML grammars.
Fixed selection of elements with relative xml:base attributes so that the resolved base URI is correct.
Fixed . Added a cx:markup-blitz step and made it possible to use either NineML or Markup Blitz for the p:invisible-xml step.
Fixed . Make sure that catalog lookup is performed when XML Schema modules are loaded.
Fixed . Remarkably, the p:urify function didn’t correctly handle “\” in the file path. This may also resolve .
Improved the error message for err:XD0049; it now includes the URI of the document that caused the error, if the URI is available.
Improved error messages generally by not losing the underlying exception and printing the underlying cause when an uncaught exception stops the pipeline.
Added an initial implementation of the cx:asciidoctor step. This implements conversion from Asciidoctor to DocBook, HTML, or PDF.
Added an initial implementation of the cx:xmlunit step. This implements document comparisons with XMLUnit. It doesn’t support everything that XMLUnit can do, but it supports many of the options.

Added an initial implementation of RDF-related steps: cx:rdf-merge, cx:rdf-graph, cx:rdfa, and cx:sparql. Added support for a wide range of RDF content types: application/ld+json, application/n-quads, application/n-triples, application/rdf+json, application/rdf+thrift, application/rdf+xml, application/sparql-query, application/sparql-results+json, application/sparql-results+xml, application/trig, text/n3, and text/turtle. (Supporting these content types means that the standard p:document instruction and the p:load and p:store steps support RDF documents natively.)
Added a number of new service provider interfaces so that extension steps can interact with the processor configuration.
Fixed a typo in the declaration of the cx:epubcheck step.
Cleaned up some whitespace, unused imports, and did some general code tidying.

revdescription.para: The 3.0.0-alpha19 release failed because of an error in build automation. This is functionally the same release.

listitem.para: Fixed . The default encoding on Windows is now Windows 1252. (It was previously documented that way, but not implemented that way.)
Fixed . The p:urify function can be called with a single argument.
Fixed . The static base URI was not being set correctly in expressions. Also updated the error message that arises if an expression fails to include location information.
Fixed . The p:validate-with-schematron step now returns a xvrl:report (not a reports). The bug that caused digest roll-ups to be incorrect has been fixed.
Fixed . That sentence in the README now has a verb.

Fixed . The help text has been updated to reflect current usage. Making the help text comprehensive seemed too verbose; the common options are summarized with a link to the documentation for more detail.
Fixed . Updated the “quick start” section of the README for clarity.
Fixed . Fixed a link accidentally broken by a global search-and-replace and a few other documentation issues.
Fixed . The --step option can be used to run any atomic step.
The error message associated with “not well formed JSON” now includes the JSON that’s being rejected. Did a bit of nearby tidying of error messages.
Updated byte order mark handling in text and JSON documents to reflect recent specification changes. (Generally, byte order marks are not part of the text.)
Tinkered with the GitHub actions: the PR builds now include the test report; the build environment includes Firefox and Chrome.
Upgraded to version 6.0.12 of the XML Resolver. This isn’t completely backwards compatible with earlier releases, so attempting to use an earlier version might not work.
Fixed . The p:lookup-uri function now queries the catalog resolver.
Fixed . Added a next command to the debugger.
Fixed . Make sure that options passed to a subpipeline are reset if the step appears in a loop.
Fixed . Correctly handle sequences of documents on the p:xslt secondary output port.
Fixed . Another XPath parsing bug. 🙁 Something more comprehensive is required.
Fixed . When a content-type is specified on p:document, it’s an override.
Fixed . Improved the error message used to report an unbound variable reference in an expression.
Fixed . Resolve the Saxon configuration file URI against the base URI of the configuration element.
Updates related to recent specification changes:
Added a p:encode step.
Adjusted the semantics of p:cast-content-type so that a c:data document is always decoded.
Added an attributes option to p:pack, p:wrap, and p:wrap-sequence.
Improved the semantics of text value templates in XML content. It’s now possible to add attributes to elements with a template.
Added a cx:collection-manager step.
Added diagramming steps (cx:ditaa, cx:mathml-to-svg, and cx:plantuml). These are published separately.
Added a cx:railroad step, published separately.
Improved error messages in several places. Improved the documentation of errors in reference pages.
Ignore serialization properties when they are explicitly set to the empty sequence.
Added support in p:cast-content-type for casting to and from text/x-java-properties. to the empty sequence.
Fixed a bug in p:viewport where the base URI of documents in the viewport was incorrect.
Allow other configuration elements in the configuration file. This provides a mechanism for steps to have their own configuration.
Improved the checking for invalid URIs.
Fixed a couple of bugs in the pipeline graph output. (Sometimes the output from a compound step wasn’t correctly connected to its input.)
Fixed issue #189. Generate an XVRL report for NVDL validation.
Fixed issue #186. Fix links to standard libraries and XProcRef.org in the reference guide.

Fixed issue #185. Check for required inputs and options before running a pipeline. When a top-level pipeline is run, check that required options and required inputs have been provided. (Checking for required inputs here is an opportunity to improve the error message.) Keep track of the required state of options until runtime. Within a pipeline, failing to provide a required option is a static error. But “top level” pipelines can’t be checked before they run. When they run, it must be possible to determine which options were declared as required.
Fixed issue #184. Fix bugs in Schematron XVRL reporting. (Generally, improve error reporting for validation steps.)

Fixed issue #160. The code was over-zealous when constructing step configurations. It created a new Saxon Configuration for every step. That’s not necessary; it’s only necessary that each p:library and p:declare-step (and their descendants) have a new configuration. Configurations are required at that level because any use of p:import-functions has to be isolated.

Compute a total order over subpipeline steps during graph building. This change replaces the, in retrospect very strange, approach previously taken where the steps were effectively unordered and at runtime each was tested to see if it could be run. Now we work out in advance a total order such that no step runs before any step that it depends on. (With some special cases to deal with the when/otherwise clauses in a choose.)
Fixed bug where buffered messages (accessible through p:pipeline-messages) could be “null” instead of the correct message.
Implemented the cx:wait-for-update step.
Implemented the cx:until and cx:while steps.
Added an “Errors and error messages” chapter to the user guide. Reworked document resolver APIs; made it possible to publish the XVRL-to-text stylesheet in the user guide.

Tidy up the pipeline/graph visualization output. Output option names for options, use the command line --debug flag to control debugging output. Use «anonymous» instead of the arbitrary step ID for the root pipeline if it has no declared type.
Fixed bug in exclude-inline-prefixes where it was possible to generate a document that was not namespace well-formed.
Fixed issue #175. Make sure directories are created before attempting to write files.

Fixed issue #174. Improved reporting of user-defined errors. If a pipeline author aborts a pipeline with p:error, make sure that any details provided are presented when the pipeline fails. (Don’t attempt to use the error explainer, it won’t know anything about that error.)

Fixed issue #173. The “detailed” option on p:directory-list didn’t work on Windows because Windows doesn’t support POSIX file permissions. On Windows, the step succeeds but provides slightly less detail.

Reworked how Graphviz visualizations are created and stored. The --description and --graph options have been replaced with a single --graphs option. The new option writes all of the descriptions to an output directory. Instead of one, potentially huge, SVG diagram of the entire set of pipelines, there are now distinct graphs for each pipeline with hyperlinks between them.
Fixed issue #167. Make sure that the --init functions are applied to every configuration.
Fixed issues #164 and #165. Improved XVRL reporting and metadata.
Fixed issue #159. Make sure that validity errors are reported in XVRL. Improve reports associated with RELAX NG validation failures.

Fixed issue #157. In p:validate-with-xml-schema, ignore any errors that arise when attempting to locate a schema at the namespace URI. (It’s not absolutely certain that this was the cause of #157, but it’s my best guess.)
Fixed issue #156 and related knock-on issues, including:
Make sure that steps wait for all of their option binding inputs. (Previous releases worked accidentally in this regard.)
Make sure the base URI of an expression is always resolved against the point of definition, not the point of use.
Only apply external option bindings to p:option instructions. (And not also p:with-option instructions!)
Make sure steps declared in libraries are always fully validated.
Fixed bug where values cast to xs:integer were returned as xs:decimal values.
Reworked how lazy bindings are managed; they’re now always documents.
General improvements to logging, trace listening, message reporting, and serialization.

Fixed issue #153. Setup the correct namespace context in p:if. A p:if is rewritten as a p:choose containing a p:when; make sure that the p:when constructed for this purpose has the right namespace context.
Fixed issue #152. Discard unused inputs on p:inline steps.
When constructing SVG graph output, ignore stylesheet errors rather than causing the processing to fail. (This hasn’t fixed the errors, but it makes it possible to ignore them in the short term.)
Found and fixed (some) issues related to how text value templates are expanded. (There are still open questions.)
Improved handling of err:XD0011. Always provide a reason.
Fix bug where namespace bindings on attributes could be lost
Attempt to manage the console output encoding.

There’s a new configuration file setting, console-output-encoding. When XML Calabash writes to the console, it attempts to assure that the output is appropriate for that encoding. There’s a bit of a messy interaction between the new “message printer” class and the existing “message reporter” class. More refactoring may be useful.
Added “piped mode” to support processing XML in a unix-style pipeline.

In piped mode (--pipe or piped-io), primary input comes from stdin by default and the primary output goes to stdout by default. Explicit bindings are still possible. The pretty printing associated with console output is disabled.
Added a (somewhat crude) PowerShell script to the distribution to run XML Calabash on Windows.
Reworked Java versions again. This release attempts to move the requirement back to Java 11, except for the “polyglot” steps which require Java 17 or later.
Fixed issue #144. The XPath parser is still a little ad hoc. Also improved the error message if this situation arises again.
Fixed issue #142. The default readable port of a step that followed a p:try, that itself had an implicit output port, was not computed correctly.

Fixed issue #141. Make sure the continuous integration build scripts use the correct documentation paths. (In order to make relative links between the guides easier to test, I moved the build directories.)
Fixed issue #140. Removed the accidental restriction that p:variable was not allowed in p:try.
Fixed issue #138. The Windows shell doesn’t support UTF-8 by default (checks calendar, yep, it is 2025) so back to plain old US ASCII for all messages by default. 🎵sad trombone🎶

Fixed issue #134. The last release (perhaps the last couple of releases) have accidentally required Java 21. This release moves the requirement back to Java 17. Java 17 is a “long-term-support” release from 2021 so it’s not exactly cutting edge. Supporting Java 8, the historical favorite, is now deprecated, so it’s time to move forward. Java 17 seems like a reasonable compromise between 11 (2018) and 21 (2023).
Fixed issue #131. Clarified documentation of the CSS and XSL formatters steps. Fixed broken links between the user guide and the reference.
Fixed issue #130. There was a typo in the Relax NG grammar for the configuration file that caused cc:mimetype to appear twice when the second occurrence should have been cc:paged-media
Fixed issue #125. Corrected the explanation of verbosity in the --help output.
Fixed issue #124. Updated the way the configuration is parsed so that the absence of the licensed attribute on the configuration isn’t interpreted as a request for a “non-licensed” configuration.
Fixed issue #123. Added a namespace declaration to the tableaux for the cc:xml-calabash configuration element.

Fixed issue #122. Added and documented the --explain command line argument. (Previously, the explanation behavior was tied to the verbosity level which doesn’t really make sense. I also fixed a bug where the stack trace was printed twice if debug verbosity was used.)
Fixed a bug where lazily evaluated expressions might have the wrong in-scope namespaces.
Fixed a bug where the schema-awareness of expressions and the schema-validity of documents could get out of sync causing errors.
Fixed a bug where a spurious option was passed to visualizers established by the configuration file.
Added Graphviz output to the debug log if generating SVG fails.
Allow the debugger breakpoint syntax to begin “break at” as well as “break on”.
Fixed an issue where the debugger was unable to inspect the document properties of step inputs.

Improved the debugger breakpoint command to check that the specified breakpoint is possible. The command will now reject attempts to set breakpoints that don’t refer to a valid step id. The model command has been extended to print all of the possible ids in a pipeline.

Tinkered with the timeout and sleep duration options in advance of some anticipated specification changes. The sleep duration is now a number of seconds, not milliseconds. Both values can be either a number or a string in the form of an xs:dayTimeDuration.
Completely refactored the code that parses and serializes documents. Added support for YAML and TOML content types.
Added cx:xpath and cx:polyglot steps (cx:javascript, cx:python, etc.).
Bumped the Java version to 21, fixed a number of deprecation warnings.
Fixed a bug where [p:]message was still not being handled correctly.
Added a cx:epubcheck step.
Updated assertions to support using an XProc pipeline as an assertion.
This release never actually happened. There was a typo in the build script. I opted to bump the version rather than moving a published tag.

Fixed issue #92. Updated the p:archive, p:archive-manifest, and p:unarchive steps to support all of the formats supported by the Apache Commons Compression library. The “create” command on p:archive also supports merging multiple archives together.
Added a “visualization” API for tracking pipeline progress. Extensively revised how logging works. Removed the now unnecessary “progress” level of verbosity.
By default system logging only goes to the console and uses dynamic levels. For a different configuration, use a different logback.xml configuration file.

Fixed bugs related to [p:]message attributes. Messages are now output through the message reporter at “info” level, rather than being printed directly to the console. Fixed a bug where static messages on compound steps were not being output at all.
Completely reworked how XVRL is supported. There’s now an internal model for the report format. Conversion from SVRL to XVRL is done by constructing the XVRL model.
Fixed issue #90 by correcting a typo in the SVG graphing stylesheet.
Fixed issue #93 by removing the accidental restriction that p:variable was not allowed in p:if. Hat tip to Achim for reporting that one!

Fixed issue #96. An option that had no default value but whose type did not allow the empty sequence was generating a compile time error about the invalid (default) value. The initializer now defers the error until runtime (where it won’t happen if a value is provided for the option).

Added application/epub+zip, application/java-archive, application/x-7z-compressed, application/x-archive, application/x-arj, application/x-cpio, and application/x-tar to the standard content type mapping.
Added an experimental xmlcalabash.sh script to the distribution. This should make it easier to run XML Calabash with a modified classpath.

Renamed a few build properties. The BUILD_HASH is now BUILD_ID and is more sensitive to internal builds. Renamed SAXON to SAXON_EDITION and removed the misleading SAXON_LICENSED property. (If you run PE or EE without a license, the edition reported is HE.)
Attempt to detect when PE or EE is running without a license and provide a more helpful version message.
Upgraded to SchXslt 1.3.1. Upgrade to jing/trang 20241231. Upgraded a few Kotlin libraries. Added the brotli and xz libraries to the core build.
Fixed a bug where the error location information for an error was getting lost.
Fixed an issue where the command line interface used by the debugger was always a “dumb” terminal. It now supports history and editing keys.
Improve the error messages associated with attempting to set inputs or outputs on the command line for ports that don’t exist in the pipeline.
An error is now reported if psvi-required is true but the processor doesn’t support XML Schema validation. (Saxon EE is required for PSVI support.)
Renamed the “schema-aware” command line option and configuration property to “licensed”. Cleaned up the tests for schema awareness in several places.
Added support for the [p:]timeout option on steps.
Added support for the timeout parameter on p:http-request.
Improved the error message associated with an undeclared prefix in an XPath expression.
Improved the error codes reported for static errors in several places.

Reworked the MessageReporter interface; allowed one reporter to chain to another. Added a buffering reporter to keep track of messages. By default the buffering reporter chains to the default reporter which chains to the logging reporter. The buffering reporter holds the last 32 messages. The default reporter prints messages to the console if they have a level that exceeds the verbosity threshold. The logging reporter sends all messages to the Java logger.
There’s a new message-buffer-size configuration setting to set the number of messages to buffered.
Added a new cx:pipeline-messages extension step that can retrieve the messages buffered by the buffering reporter.
Changed the message reporter and document manager to be unique per-pipeline, rather than shared across multiple pipelines.
Fixed a bug where serialization properties on p:output were not being applied when pipeline outputs were serialized.
Fixed a bug where XML Calabash was failing to detect that p:import must precede p:input and p:output. Fixed that error in many of the tests in the extra test suite.
Improved support for Schematron assertions. Assertions are now applied to non-XML values by first performing “cast content type” on them.

Added support for a cx:href attribute on p:pipeinfo. When present, the processor behaves as if the referenced document appeared where the reference appears. The p:pipeinfo must be empty and the cx:href must point to a p:pipeinfo document. This makes it practical to share Schematron assertions across pipelines.
“Fixed” #74 by adding a hack to the manifest classpath.
Fixed an obscure bug in the debug logging message associated with p:sleep.
Upgraded from SchXslt1 to SchXslt2 version 1.3.
Cleaned up the error reporter in many steps.
Removed the defunct debug configuration setting.
Improve the reference documentation for steps. Defer to the specification and to Erik Siegal’s excellent XProcRef for standard step descriptions.
Added the Schematron assertions feature.
Added a catch command to the debugger to catch steps that fail. Added an option to the step command to stop after a step executes.
Fixed a bug in the way steps are handled in nested, common imports.
